1.label: Solo Queue
1.description: You can't rely on teammates for coordination. Pick operators that can open their own paths, gather their own intel, and frag independently. Avoid hard support roles — your team probably won't follow up on your utility.
priorities: Pick operators with frag grenades or self-sufficient gadgets
Drone for yourself — don't expect teammates to drone you in
Play for trades, not solo entries — follow a teammate's push
Avoid hard breach unless nobody else picks it (then you must)
Use your mic for basic callouts even if nobody responds

2.label: Duo Queue
2.description: One of you entries, the other drones and supports. This is the most impactful duo setup — you can win gunfights your solo queue teammates never could. Coordinate your operator picks before the round.
priorities: One player drones, the other entries off that intel
Split roles: one fragger + one support/flex operator
Coordinate utility — e.g., one brings flashes, other brings smokes
Call out for each other and play off the same area of the map
Let randoms fill hard breach/support — take the impactful roles

3.label: 3-Stack
3.description: Three coordinated players can run a real execute. Assign entry, support, and flex roles. You control the pace of the round — the two randoms will follow your lead if you're decisive.
priorities: Assign roles before the round: entry, support, flex
Run a planned execute on one side of the map
One player handles hard breach or key utility
One player drones and calls, one entries
Third player watches flank or plays vertical
avoidRoles: All three on the same role

4.label: 4-Stack
4.description: Four players is enough to run a complete strat. Cover hard breach, entry, support, and flex. The random fifth will usually fill — don't rely on them for critical utility.
priorities: Run the full strat — you have enough players to execute properly
Assign the random a simple role or let them freelance
Coordinate all utility usage and timing
One dedicated IGL makes the calls, others execute
Save one player for post-plant or late-round anchor
avoidRoles: Leaving critical roles to the random

5.label: Full Stack

priorities: Follow the operator lineup and strategy exactly
IGL calls the execute timing and rotations
Pre-planned drone routes and utility sequences
Everyone knows their role, position, and job
Adapt mid-round based on intel — call audibles together
bestRoles: All roles covered as shown in lineup

reinforce: Ground rule: there is no ceiling hatch above 2F Kids' Dorms — confirmed in game. Nothing gets reinforced overhead and no claw goes on a ceiling. Reinforcing is prep-phase only; if it isn't placed when the clock flips, it isn't happening.

1. AARON — the hatch in the Kids' Dorms floor, beside the bunk. It drops straight into 1F Kitchen, so leaving it open hands them a route up into the site from a room they may already be attacking. One reinforcement kills the entire from-below plan.
2. AARON — the wall between 2F Kids' Dorms and 2F Dorms Main Hall. Widest same-floor entry and the first thing a hard breacher picks.
3. JACKSON — the exterior-facing wall of 2F Kids' Dorms that attackers reach off EXT Meeting Hall Roof. Same floor for them, no climbing, and it's the wall duos forget.

4. JACKSON — his second goes on whatever else in the site is reinforceable and faces a room you are not holding. We have not confirmed how many reinforceable walls this site actually has, so walk it in prep round one. If there is no sensible fourth, he holds it rather than spending it badly — an unspent reinforcement beats a wall that boxes you in.
The two randoms cover anything left over. Nobody spends one overhead.
job: Prep, first thing: walk down to 1F Kitchen and put one cam on it, covering the ground under the bunk hatch. That is the room they come up from — the cam is your early warning that they are stacking under you.
Cam two out the 2F Kids' Dorms window looking onto EXT Meeting Hall Roof. Same-floor entry with no climb for them, and it's the one that goes unwatched.

Cam three high in 2F Dorms Main Hall, angled down the length of the hall and covering the top of 2F Tower Stairs. Point it down the hall, not at the door — you want them walking into frame, not already on top of it.
Spend your two reinforcements in order: the floor hatch, then the 2F Dorms Main Hall wall.
Round start you are the voice. Call which side the drones came from and whether bodies are gathering in 1F Kitchen below the bunk hatch or crossing 2F.
Short roam only: 2F Dorms Main Hall and the top of 2F Tower Stairs to punish the stair push. One angle, one trade, back inside. You're playing utility here, not entry — don't go hunting.
Fall-back trigger: the first hard-breach charge goes on a wall, or you take fire from two directions. Reset into the site on either. Don't buy the hall with your body.
duoJob: Four GC90 jammers. All four go down in prep and then you never think about them again.
Jammer 1 on the reinforced bunk hatch — that denies a breach charge on it from 1F Kitchen below.
Jammer 2 covering the reinforced 2F Kids' Dorms / 2F Dorms Main Hall wall. Place it inside the site tight against that wall so it can't be shot out from the hall side.
Jammer 3 on the window side facing EXT Meeting Hall Roof. Eats drones coming in that way and covers that reinforced wall.
Jammer 4 out in 2F Dorms Main Hall to kill early drones before they ever see the site.
Spread them out. Thatcher carries three EMPs — if two of your jammers sit in one blast radius he pays one grenade for both.
Your two reinforcements are #3 and #4 on the list. Place them, then anchor and that's it. You don't chase, you don't rotate for a kill, you don't go find the drone you heard.
Your trigger is a body crossing the doorway. Pre-aim head height and let them walk into it.
defense.anchor: your duo sits in the deep corner of 2F Kids' Dorms diagonally opposite the door from 2F Dorms Main Hall, crouched behind furniture. One job in that corner: gun up at head height on that doorway before the action phase starts. If the defuser ends up outside that view, he does not turn for it — you covers the plant, your duo covers the door. The corner is chosen for the longest sightline onto the same-floor entry. He does not leave it for anything short of the fallback call.
defense.fallback: Trigger: the 2F Dorms Main Hall wall opens, or both randoms are down. your duo does not move — he stays in the deep corner as the last gun covering the defuser. you does not stack in that corner with him; he peels into 2F Dorms Main Hall and holds the hall side of the hole so anyone stepping through gets shot from behind. Two guns on two different sides of the same hole beats two guns in one corner. If the defuser goes down and the site is lost, you plays the retake from 2F Dorms Main Hall through the hole they made and your duo calls the defuser position — one peek at a time, never both at once.
defense.roam: you only, and no further than 2F Dorms Main Hall and the top of 2F Tower Stairs. Two-man top-floor site — nobody deep-roams to 1F or the basement. If you isn't back inside by the time a hard-breach charge is placed, this becomes a solo hold and it's a lost round.
defense.randoms: Ask them for three things and nothing else: one body covering 2F Tower Stairs / 2F Big Tower so nobody walks in behind you, one covering 1F Kitchen, which is directly under the bunk hatch, and any spare reinforcements on Kids' Dorms walls the two of you didn't get to. One line in comms on the hatch: leave the floor hatch alone until you has reinforced it, and once it's up nobody tries to open it.

attack.spawn: Junkyard. Both of you spawn the same side and travel together — no split. Junkyard gets you onto EXT Meeting Hall Roof and into 2F on the same floor as the site, which is the whole plan: there is no ceiling hatch above 2F Kids' Dorms, so every route is same-floor or up from 1F.
approach: Frame the round correctly before you move: this is a same-floor hard breach into 2F Kids' Dorms from 2F Dorms Main Hall. The bunk hatch — in the site's floor, dropping to 1F Kitchen — is the pressure valve, not the entry.

Drone phase out of Junkyard. you drones 2F Dorms Main Hall and the site — find the Mute jammers, find the anchor's corner, confirm whether the Dorms Main Hall wall is reinforced. your duo keeps his drone alive and parks it in 2F Dorms Main Hall for the entry.

Climb onto EXT Meeting Hall Roof and enter 2F through the window into 2F Dorms Main Hall. Clear the hall before anyone touches a wall — a roamer behind you ends this round faster than the anchor will.
Own the hall. you faces 2F Tower Stairs and 2F Big Tower watching the flank while your duo sets up on the wall.
you EMPs the jammer covering the breach wall and says 'EMP out' on comms. Three EMPs total: one for that jammer, one held for a second jammer or an electrified wall, one saved for post-plant.

Ace opens the wall. Nobody runs through it. your duo holds the hole at head height from the hall side, you holds the flank, and you either let the anchor come to the hole or you drone the deep corner first.
Enter together on your call, clear the deep corner diagonal from the doorway, then plant.
job: You are utility, not entry. You do not lead through the hole at any point in this round.
Drone first and report honestly. Jammer positions are the round — call each one by the wall it covers, not 'there's a jammer somewhere.'

You own all three EMPs. One clears the breach wall, one stays in pocket for a second jammer or an electrified wall, one is for post-plant on a cam or a Kapkan EDD near the defuser. Kapkan traps only trigger on you, so clearing them before the plant is worth the grenade.
Throw the breach EMP from inside 2F Dorms Main Hall, close enough that it lands past the jammer, and call it out loud before it detonates. your duo's charge waits on that call.
Once the wall is open your gun points down 2F Dorms Main Hall toward 2F Tower Stairs. You're the flank watch; your duo has the hole.
Watch the window side off EXT Meeting Hall Roof after you've entered — same floor means they can come back around the way you came.
Post-plant you stay on the hall angle. You do not both stand inside the room staring at the defuser.
duoJob: One job: put a SELMA charge on the wall the drone marked, and only after you hear 'EMP out.' Never before.
If a jammer is still live the charge is dead on the wall. Waiting for your call is the only decision you make all round — everything else is aim.
Ace charges also open the reinforced bunk hatch from 1F Kitchen below. That is the backup route and it goes off only on your call, not on your own idea.
Once the wall is open, hold the hole at head height from the hall side. You're the trigger on that angle, not the runner.
Enter on your call, clear the deep corner diagonal from the doorway, then get on the defuser while you holds 2F Dorms Main Hall.
No laser sight on the gun you're holding that angle with — it gives your position away the moment you ADS on the hole.
attack.plant: Plant inside 2F Kids' Dorms against the wall you just opened, low behind furniture, so the defuser sits in the open lane between your hole and the deep corner. your duo plants, you holds 2F Dorms Main Hall. The second it's down, both of you get back out through the hole and hold the hall side of it — you defend the defuser through the wall you made, not from inside the room where one retake or one runout catches you both standing together.
attack.ifStalled: If 2F Dorms Main Hall is locked down and you're bleeding clock on the wall, go under the site instead of forcing it. Ace puts a charge on the bunk hatch and blows it open from 1F Kitchen below. Do not climb up through it; that's a free kill for the anchor. Open it, your duo holds it from below so the deep corner and the plant area are no longer safe to sit in, and you re-enters alone from 2F Dorms Main Hall while the anchor is turned the wrong way. Still stuck after that: take it as a hall fight. Hold 2F Dorms Main Hall, make them leave the site to contest you, and plant late.

uncertain: How many walls in 2F Kids' Dorms are genuinely reinforceable versus already solid. The priority order holds either way, but the count might not, and your duo's second reinforcement depends on it.

Whether the window off EXT Meeting Hall Roof puts you directly into 2F Dorms Main Hall or into a room off it. Confirm on the first attack round so the entry call is exact.
Whether anything on 2F outside the site (2F Trophy Room, 2F Attic, 2F Big Tower) has a sightline into 2F Kids' Dorms once the main wall is open — worth one drone to find out.

There is no ceiling hatch above the site — that is confirmed. What is NOT confirmed is whether the ceiling is soft enough to shoot or vertical-breach through. Nobody has checked, so nothing in this plan assumes either way.

The hatch above the site (reinforced from the room above, 2F Dorms Main Hall / 2F Kids' Dorms side). One of you runs up in the first 15 seconds and does this before anything else — you will not get time later.
The wall between 1F Dining Hall and the corridor running toward 1F Meeting Hall. This is the flat rotate attackers use once they drop through the 1F Meeting Hall roof hatch.
Fourth panel: a second bay on the Kitchen exterior wall, so a single Thermite charge doesn't open the whole face.
job: Run up and reinforce the hatch above the site first — before you place a single gadget. Come straight back down.

Claw #1 goes on the CEILING under that reinforced hatch, thrown from below, so you electrify the hatch without standing on the floor above. Assume a Twitch drone can angle up and reach it: place it so the drone has to push into the room and expose itself to your angle to take the shot, and be ready to re-throw if it gets eaten.
Claw #2 goes on the reinforced Kitchen exterior wall, on the panel closest to the plant side.
Anchor and call. your job all round is 'they're above me' / 'wall's being charged' / 'drone in Dining'. your duo reacts to your voice, so make the calls short and say the room name.
duoJob: Spend roughly half your kunai at prep — one sealing the exterior window/soft-wall approach into 1F Kitchen, one on the doorway you do NOT want to defend, so you only have to watch one entrance.

Save the rest. That is the whole point of you being on Azami. The moment the ceiling opens above the site, throw a kiba straight up into the hole. Do not shoot first, do not peek the hole, patch it and step off the angle.
A patched hole is bulletproof — they cannot shoot it back open. It comes down to explosives or a Twitch dart, so don't stand under a barrier you just placed and don't assume it's permanent.
Hold ONE angle: the doorway between 1F Kitchen and 1F Dining Hall, ADS pre-aimed at head height, from a corner that isn't lit by the hole above.
After you patch a hole, count two seconds and re-peek from a different position than the one you patched from.
If you dies, you don't chase the trade. Patch, hold, and let them come to your angle.
defense.anchor: you anchors in 1F Kitchen in the back corner diagonal from the Dining Hall doorway, with the reinforced exterior wall on his shoulder and a sightline that covers both the doorway and the ceiling over the plant-side wall. your duo anchors the same room but on the opposite corner so the two of you cover the doorway from two angles — no stacking behind the same object.
defense.fallback: Trigger: the ceiling is open in two places AND your duo is out of kunai, or you hear the plant start. Do not trade into the hole. Both of you pull into the other half of the site (Kitchen if you lost Dining, Dining if you lost Kitchen), swap to opposite sides of the connecting doorway, and force them to enter a doorway instead of dropping on you. If the site has a hatch down to the basement, that's your second option: drop, run the basement, and come back up behind the plant from the other stairwell — but only with 25+ seconds on the defuser, otherwise you're just donating the round.
defense.roam: Neither of you roams. you anchors, your duo anchors, the randoms roam.
defense.randoms: Ask for three things, in this order. One: somebody plays the floor directly above the site (2F Dorms Main Hall / 2F Kids' Dorms) and does not leave until the first attacker dies up there — the site is lost from above, not through the doorways. Two: one roamer on the 1F Meeting Hall / 1F Lobby side for a timing pick, back to site at 45 seconds, no exceptions. Three: spend their reinforcements on the exterior faces you didn't get, and if anyone is on Mute or Bandit, put denial on the Kitchen exterior wall — a Mute has four disruptors, so there is no reason for that wall to be uncovered. Say it once in prep, don't repeat it.

attack.spawn: Junkyard, both of you, same spawn. As a two-man you never split spawns — let the randoms make noise on the other faces. Junkyard is the shortest exterior walk to the roof/upper access and it keeps your drone and your duo's climb on the same clock. If in a custom you find the climb is faster from Construction Site, take that instead — the route matters, not the spawn name.
approach: Prep phase: you sends one drone to the site and does NOT drive it into the room. Park it in a dark corner of 1F Dining Hall pointed at the 1F Kitchen doorway. That drone is your eyes for the entire round. Keep the second drone in his pocket for post-plant.

Before anyone moves, you gives one sentence: how many bodies in the site, whether the ceiling is electrified (Kaid claw), and whether the Kitchen exterior wall is reinforced. If that wall is soft, throw this plan out and just enter through it.

your duo climbs to the floor directly above the site (2F Dorms Main Hall / 2F Kids' Dorms) and STOPS. He clears the room he's standing in first. The number one way this play dies is a defender already sitting up there with him.

you spends darts before the floor opens, in this order: Kaid claw on the hatch, then Wamai/ADS, then Thorn traps and cameras. Melusi only if he can get behind or above the Banshee. Every dart spent here is a free hole for your duo.

Trigger to open: you says a number out loud — 'two below, open.' your duo opens TWO holes, one over each half of the site, spaced far enough apart that a defender standing under one cannot cover the other — opposite ends of the room, not two holes in the same ceiling panel.

your duo holds hole one, you re-drones and watches hole two. Nobody drops until two defenders have been called dead or displaced. Vertical damage is the point — you are not obligated to enter at all if they're bleeding out below you.

Entry: drop through the hole nearest the wall you intend to plant against. your duo goes first because he's the better shot in a close-range trade; you drops last with the drone out so he lands already looking at the rotate doorway.
Randoms get one instruction: hold the 1F rotates so nobody walks back in on you — one on the corridor toward 1F Meeting Hall, one on the basement stairs side.
job: Drone discipline: one drone into the site early and parked, one saved for post-plant.
Dart priority is gadgets that stop the vertical, not gadgets that annoy you. Kaid claw on the hatch first. Always.
Keep at least one dart in reserve for a kiba. If Azami patches one of your duo's holes, the dart is how it comes back down — nobody is shooting it open.
Once holes are open, reposition so you can see the hole your duo is not watching. Your kill on someone repositioning under the second hole is the kill that wins this.
Call bodies by room name, short: 'one Kitchen', 'two Dining'. No paragraphs mid-fight.
Post-plant: drone the retake lane, not the defuser. your duo watches the defuser, you watch where they'll come from.
duoJob: Clear the room above the site before you touch the floor. Corners first, then look down.
Open on your call, not on your own timer. Two holes, spaced — never one big hole you both stare into.
After opening: do not stand on the hole. Take one step back, let them look up at nothing, then shoot down from an angle they can't pre-fire.

If Azami patches a hole, do not shoot it. A kiba barrier is bulletproof — Skeleton Key does nothing to it. Call it, let you dart it down, and while you wait open a fresh hole a few feet away instead of hunting for another route.
When you drop, you're the first body in. Land, immediately turn to the doorway of the room you landed in, and let you cover behind you.
attack.plant: Plant in 1F Kitchen, tight against the reinforced exterior wall, on the half of the room that your duo's hole covers — so the hole above is watching the defuser and the only retake angles left are the two doorways you already have crossfired. If the Kitchen half is stacked, plant in 1F Dining Hall instead, against the wall shared with the Kitchen. Rule of thumb: plant on the side of the site whose ceiling you own, never in the middle of the open floor.
attack.ifStalled: If they've denied the ceiling — Kaid claw you can't reach, an Azami sealing every hole, a defender contesting the room above — stop feeding bodies into the floor. Go flat: use the EXT Meeting Hall Roof hatch to drop into 1F Meeting Hall and push the corridor into 1F Dining Hall while the randoms hold the other face. If you know before the round starts that the ceiling is their whole plan, you swaps Twitch for Thatcher or Maverick and you attack the reinforced Kitchen exterior wall directly instead — Maverick specifically, because it opens the wall without Kaid getting a say. On Thatcher you have three EMPs; one is enough for a single claw-covered wall, so do not plan a route that needs a fourth.

reinforce: ROUND ONE, BEFORE YOU SPEND ANYTHING: look up in Meeting Hall and check whether there is actually a ceiling hatch there. Nobody has confirmed it, and the identical assumption on 2F Kids' Dorms turned out to be false. IF IT IS THERE: reinforce it first, every round, no exceptions — an open hatch means they fight you from a place you cannot shoot back into. IF IT IS NOT: skip straight to the exterior wall below, tell me, and I will rewrite this page.
The exterior wall panels of Meeting Hall facing EXT Construction Site. That is the hard-breach wall from the closest spawn. Second reinforce if the hatch exists, FIRST if it does not.

The Kitchen side of the wall Kitchen shares with 1F Dining Hall, so the only way in from Dining Hall is the doorway your randoms are already watching. If you need that soft wall as a rotate, leave one panel and SAY IT OUT LOUD so nobody sprints into a reinforcement.

Leftovers go on the floor hatch in Kitchen down to the basement. Low priority — nobody reaches the basement in the first minute — but a spare panel there stops a late Buck or Sledge opening it behind you.
job: First eight seconds: look up. If the Meeting Hall ceiling hatch is real, reinforce it now. If it is not, put that reinforcement on the exterior wall instead and say so on comms.

Claw #1 goes on the hatch if it exists — on the adjacent wall or ceiling, not out on the open Meeting Hall floor where a drone or a hole from above pops it before the round starts. No hatch: claw #1 goes on the exterior reinforcement instead.

Hold claw #2 through prep. You do not yet know if they are committing roof or wall. When your duo calls drones on the Construction Site side, claw the exterior reinforcement; if you hear them stacking above you, save it to re-claw the hatch after their EMPs land.
Anchor in Kitchen, not in Meeting Hall. Meeting Hall is too big a room to hold from inside it — make them cross the connector between the two rooms instead.
Once both claws are gone and you hear EMPs, stop playing the wall entirely. Back to your Kitchen angle and let them walk to you.
Callouts are your job: where the hole opened, how many came through, how many are still outside.
duoJob: Jammer 1 directly under the Meeting Hall ceiling hatch, tucked against a wall so a drone on the roof cannot see it.
Jammer 2 covering the reinforced exterior wall on the EXT Construction Site side — placed inside the room and off to one side, never centred on the wall where a nade through the breach kills it.
Jammer 3 in Kitchen near the Dining Hall doorway. That one is purely a drone-killer for the interior push.
Jammer 4 on the Kitchen floor hatch. If that hatch turns out not to exist, put it on the second approach into Meeting Hall instead. All four go down in prep — you do not carry one in reserve.

Then stop moving. Hold the Meeting Hall corner furthest from the breach wall with an angle onto it. You shoot the first body through the hole and then you leave — do not hold that angle for a second fight, they will have the trade lined up.
Your trigger to leave Meeting Hall: the hatch above you opens, OR you hear two EMPs. Walk the connector into Kitchen and set up beside you. Never try to retake Meeting Hall on your own.
defense.anchor: 1F Kitchen, in the corner that holds the connector doorway from 1F Meeting Hall — deep enough that a frag thrown through the Meeting Hall breach hole cannot reach you.
defense.fallback: Trigger: the plant goes down in Meeting Hall, or both of you are down to one body in there. Then everyone lives in Kitchen — you on the connector, your duo on the Dining Hall doorway — and you only retake through the connector at roughly 15 seconds on the defuser, with a nade or a random going through first. If the plant is in Kitchen instead, fall back into 1F Dining Hall and retake through the doorway plus the soft wall together; do not run back in through the connector, that is the one angle they are already holding.
defense.roam: Neither of you roams. you anchors Kitchen all round; your duo anchors Meeting Hall then collapses to Kitchen on his trigger. Give the roam to a random with a 20-second leash and tell him not to chase spawn.
defense.randoms: Ask for exactly three things, in this order: one hard anchor who stays inside Meeting Hall the whole round, one roamer who delays from the 1F Lobby / 1F Security Corridor side on a short leash, and one body in 1F Dining Hall watching the Kitchen doorway. If anyone has Valkyrie, ask for a cam in Meeting Hall and one on the EXT Construction Site side — neither of you is bringing intel this round.

attack.spawn: EXT Construction Site. Closest spawn to the Meeting Hall exterior wall and the only one that keeps the roof option live without a 40-second run. From EXT Junkyard or Street you are attacking the Kitchen half through the building, which is a five-man coordinated job, not a two-man job.
approach: you drives the exterior of Meeting Hall checking two things only — is the EXT Construction Site wall reinforced, and is the ceiling hatch reinforced. your duo parks his drone where it can see the Kitchen doorway and leaves it alive for the round.
you walks up to the exterior wall. your duo sets up 8-10m back with an angle onto it — not standing next to you. If a Kapkan trap pops or someone runs out, your duo takes that fight.

EMPs go one at a time, not all three at once. After the first, you calls what he heard — a Kaid claw popping and a Mute jammer popping are different sounds. If nothing popped, the wall was never electrified and you still have two EMPs.
your duo breaches only on the words 'wall's clean.' Two SELMAs on adjacent panels, aimed low so you get a doorway and not a window you have to vault through.

Nobody entries the hole first. you holds the outside angle so nobody runs out behind you; your duo holds the hole from an angle and shoots the first defender who peeks. Push a random in first, or push together after you've traded one.
Once inside, you are not clearing Meeting Hall. Cross to the Kitchen-side wall and set the plant there — a room that size takes more than two bodies to clear and the clock will not cover it.
Randoms get three one-line jobs: one pressures Kitchen from 1F Dining Hall all round so the defenders cannot stack Meeting Hall, one watches the flank toward EXT Bus Yard, one drones for the plant.
job: Drone first, EMP second, gun third. You are not the entry on this site.
You have three EMPs. Spend one per confirmed device, and keep one back in case you have to switch to the hatch.
Hold the outside long angle while your duo breaches — a runout from the Meeting Hall exterior door catches him mid-SELMA.
Call the plant out loud: which corner, who covers the connector, who covers your own breach hole. Then you personally watch the connector while the defuser goes down.
duoJob: Do not throw a SELMA until you says the wall is clean. One SELMA on an electrified panel is gone for nothing.
Two on adjacent panels, placed low. You want to walk through the hole, not climb it under fire.
Hold the hole from an angle outside it, never standing in it. Your 55.6% headshot rate is worth more on a defender peeking a fixed hole than on clearing a room.
Third SELMA stays in your pocket: it is for the ceiling hatch if the wall stalls, or for the Kitchen wall if you end up planting there instead.
attack.plant: In Meeting Hall, tight against the wall it shares with Kitchen, on the side away from the connector doorway — that puts the defuser out of the ceiling hatch's line and out of the sightline through your own breach hole. If Meeting Hall is genuinely locked down, plant in Kitchen instead, behind the counter block on the Dining Hall side.
attack.ifStalled: Two dead EMPs and a jammer you cannot find means the wall is not happening — stop feeding it. At 1:20, switch to the roof: get up onto EXT Meeting Hall Roof, you EMPs the hatch, your duo's third SELMA opens it, and you fight down while the randoms keep the exterior hole hot. If the roof climb is contested too, abandon Meeting Hall completely and take Kitchen from 1F Dining Hall with the randoms — a plant in Kitchen counts the same, and by then the defenders will often have spent their utility on the wrong room.

How you actually get onto EXT Meeting Hall Roof from EXT Construction Site — ladder vs. needing a boost. Check it in a custom before the roof plan is trusted as a real backup. If it needs a gadget: your duo swaps to Osa, you swaps to Osa or Amaru (Amaru is in your pool only — never your duo's).

reinforce: Hatch over B Laundry Room first - the one that drops down from 1F Kitchen. Put the panel on it before you place anything else; reinforcing is prep-phase only, so if you run out of time you cannot fix it later.
The other basement hatch second (the one that lands next to B Supply Room). It gets forgotten because the Kitchen hatch eats everyone's attention, and a random will happily leave it open.

The exterior-facing wall of B Supply Room - the one shared with the stairwell coming down from EXT Bunker. Low priority, and it's on the unverified list - it may not be reinforcable at all. Only spend a panel there once both hatches are done.
Do NOT reinforce the wall between B Laundry Room and B Supply Room. Blow it open in prep so the two of you can trade through it.
job: Prep: first electroclaw goes straight up into the hatch under 1F Kitchen so the panel itself is live. Throw it from underneath - you want the attacker to have to commit to killing it.
Second claw on the other hatch. Stand back and check the spark line before you walk off; if it isn't visibly arcing across the panel, pick it up and re-throw.
Burn your prep drone down B Basement Corridor to see what the randoms actually placed. If that lane is already covered by someone's trap, you stop worrying about it and stay on your angle.
In round you sit deep in B Supply Room, ADS on the hole you opened into B Laundry Room. You are not watching the corridor - your duo has it. You kill whatever steps into Laundry, nothing else.
Trigger to speak: the second a claw dies, say 'claw down.' That's hard breach in the next 10-15 seconds. Both of you get off the line under that hatch so the drop-in isn't landing on top of you.
duoJob: Jammer 1 under the 1F Kitchen hatch, set off the direct drop line so a grenade or a dropping attacker doesn't land on top of it.
Jammer 2 under the second hatch, same rule.
Jammer 3 just inside the doorway from B Basement Corridor. That one is for drones - if they can't drone the room, they can't see your angle before they walk into it.
Jammer 4 in B Supply Room covering the opened wall and the plant corner, so a drone can't scout your angle and a breach charge on that side won't arm.
In round: hard cover in B Laundry Room, one angle only, the corridor doorway. Make them walk into it.
Your only triggers to leave that angle: you calls 'claw down,' or you hear one of your jammers die. Then you reset back through the opened wall into B Supply Room and hold the hole beside him.
If the defuser goes down and you're alone, do not run at it. Hold the hole and wait for your call.
defense.anchor: Diagonal pair - you deep in B Supply Room on the opened wall, your duo in B Laundry Room on the corridor door. Anything entering either room is in two crossing angles, and neither of you can be traded for free because whoever kills one is already exposed to the other.
defense.fallback: Trigger: both hatches open, or either of you dies. Stop defending the room. Peel into B Laundry Storage (or whichever small pocket adjoins your room) and let them plant. You've traded 'two doors, one gun each' for 'one door, two guns, and a defuser whose exact location you know.' Retake through the wall you opened in prep, never back through the door you just gave up.
defense.roam: Neither of you roams. Kaid and Mute spend their value in prep and then need to be alive on site. If a random insists on roaming, point him at 1F Kitchen - the fight over the hatch above your head is the fight that decides this site.
defense.randoms: Ask for three things, one sentence each: someone brings cams (Valkyrie or Echo) and puts one in B Basement Corridor; someone contests 1F Kitchen instead of standing on site with you, so the hatch never opens for free; someone takes first contact at B Blue Bunker / the corridor. And say up front: do not reinforce the wall between B Laundry Room and B Supply Room.

attack.spawn: Junkyard. You want the side of the building where EXT Bunker and the 1F room above site sit on the same approach, so the two of you never split to threaten both. If a custom shows Junkyard is the far side, run the identical plan from EXT Construction Site - this plan is about the hatch, not the spawn.
approach: First 30 seconds is droning, not walking. you finds the jammers and the claw before anyone commits. Do not push the bunker doors early - that hallway is where every trap on this site lives.
Get up to the 1F room over the site while the randoms hold 1F Dining Hall and the stairs behind you. You two need one room, not the floor.

you pings the hatch and throws the EMP onto the panel. Confirm it worked before you spend anything else: the claw's arc stops and your duo's charge sticks. If the charge still gets denied, the EMP is not reaching the gadgets through the intact floor - get an EMP into the room below from a position with line of sight, or go to the ground route.
your duo places SELMA the instant the EMP pops. Don't wait for a verbal; the window is short and a charge placed a second early is a charge wasted.
Nobody drops yet. Open the hole, step off it, throw utility down and make the anchor move. First man through a hatch is a free kill for whoever's sitting in the corner.
Open the second hatch the same way - your second EMP, your duo's second charge. Two holes means the anchor can't watch both, and that split is what wins the site, not the drop.
Once both holes are open and their utility is spent: one of you goes down while the other holds the hole from above. Plant first if the room is quiet, clear second.
job: Own the drone all round. Drone the corridor and both rooms before your duo moves, and call traps by room and side - 'Kapkan, Laundry door, left frame.'
You have three EMPs. One for the first hatch, one for the claw on the second hatch, and hold the third for a gadget over the plant corner or for the ground route if the ceiling plan dies.
Call the anchor's position off drone footage before your duo drops. 'He's on the corridor door' is worth more than any frag you'd get swinging.
duoJob: Charge order: first hatch, then second hatch. If you still have a charge after both are open, keep it for whatever needs opening near the plant corner.
Wait for 'EMP down' before you place. Placing into a live jammer is how the charge disappears and the round dies with it.
When you go in, go second and take the opposite angle from wherever you is looking. Never both clear the same corner.
If you get the first kill on the drop, say the number and stop pushing. Hold what you took.
attack.plant: Plant in B Laundry Room, in the corner the corridor doorway can't see, directly under the hole you opened. Whoever holds that hole from above is then also covering the defuse, and any defender who wants to contest has to expose himself to the hatch to do it.
attack.ifStalled: If the ceiling plan is dead - claws replaced faster than you can EMP, or your randoms are already gone - stop paying for it and switch to the ground route: your remaining EMP into the corridor doorway lane to strip the jammer and any electric trap, your duo leads with a grenade and swings behind it, and you stays above holding the open hatch so the anchor can't rotate to the door. Plant in the open the moment the room is clear and defend the corner. Do not try to clear both rooms with two men and no clock.

reinforce: First: the exterior-facing wall of 2F Meeting Room that a player standing on EXT Garage Roof can reach. Second: the exterior-facing wall of 2F Consul Office on that same outside face. Same reason. If your randoms only give you two panels, these are the two.

Third: the wall shared between 2F Meeting Room and 2F Secretary. That is the wall a team coming up the stairs soft-breaches straight into the site. Reinforcing it does not stop a hard breach but it makes the stair route cost them real utility instead of one Sledge swing.

Fourth, and only if you have decided against the rotate hole below: the wall shared between 2F Consul Office and 2F Consul Side Room. A shotgun cannot open a reinforced panel, so this wall is either a rotate or a reinforcement. Default to the rotate, because that wall is how you get into the side room for the fallback — read the fallback before you spend a panel here.

Leave the connection between 2F Consul Office and 2F Meeting Room open. That is your rotate and your mutual cover. Do not let a random panel it, and do not panel it yourself because it looks like a hole in your setup. Two players covering two rooms only works if you can see each other.
Ask a random with a shotgun to open one low rotate hole in the Consul Office wall toward 2F Consul Side Room, at crouch height. That is your escape lane.
job: Cam one goes out a window onto EXT Garage Roof in prep. Aim it flat at the ledge attackers actually have to cross. That cam is the whole reason you picked Valkyrie here — it turns the roof route from a surprise into a countdown.
Cam two covers the stair approach — 2F Service Stairs or 2F Spiral Stairs. Ask the randoms in prep which stairwell they are holding and put the cam on the other one.
Keep the third cam. Throw it mid-round into whatever room they have taken, once you know where they are actually coming from.
Call in counts and a direction: 'one on the roof', 'two, they're stacking', 'they left the roof'.

Play the Meeting Room side, off to the side of the reinforced outside wall. Hold the angle a man has to step into after he comes through, not the hole itself. Staring at a fresh hole gets you flashed or pre-fired.
Drop off the cams the second they are in the room. Once contact starts you are the anchor holding an angle, and watching a cam while someone is pushing you gets you killed.
duoJob: Prep phase: two Kiba barriers on the windows attackers rappel or vault into. They are bulletproof — a shotgun will not open them, only explosives, hard breach, melee, or a Twitch drone. That does not stop entry, it costs them time and makes noise you can hear.
Keep at least two barriers back for mid-round. When a wall gets opened, you seal the hole from across the room and back off — never place a barrier while standing next to the hole.

Anchor deep in 2F Consul Office, in the corner that sees the doorway and the open connection to 2F Meeting Room but not the outside wall face. Sights already up on the doorway before the action phase starts.
Do not chase noise. Not a drone, not a footstep above, not a breach charge on the far side. Your job is one corner and two angles.
You move when you calls he is down, or calls two attackers through the wall. Then you shift to cover the connection into 2F Meeting Room. Any other sound, you stay put.
If they plant while you are alive and unpushed, do not solo the hole. Hold your corner and wait for you or a random to trade with you.
defense.anchor: Split the two rooms. your duo deep in 2F Consul Office on the doorway; you in 2F Meeting Room off the reinforced outside wall. You are within calling distance through the open connection, so a push into either room can be traded by the other. Neither of you should be standing where you can see the outside face directly — hold the interior angles and let them come to you.
defense.fallback: When the site opens from two faces at once, stop trying to hold both rooms. Both of you go into 2F Consul Side Room and hold the single doorway back toward 2F Consul Office. You are giving them the plant on purpose — they still have to clear that doorway or eat the retake with the defuser burning. Trigger to fall back: a second hole appears, or you calls three attackers inside.
defense.roam: No deep roams from either of you. you takes a short delay position on the 2F Catering side at the start of the action phase to catch a fast stair push, then pulls straight back to Meeting Room the moment a drone dies near the site or a breach charge goes on the outside wall. your duo never leaves the site, not once, not for a lurker.
defense.randoms: Ask for three things in order. One: a wall-denial operator — Bandit, Kaid or Mute — dedicated to the two exterior reinforcements, not roaming with them. Two: an anchor with a shotgun who opens the one low rotate hole and then names in prep which stairwell he is holding, so you can cam the other one. Three: one real roamer working 1F Yellow Stairs and B Garage to slow the ground route. If nobody takes wall denial, you drops Valkyrie for Kaid and you lose your cams — that trade is worth it, because an unprotected reinforcement on the roof face is a free hole every round.

you crosses first and calls the room. your duo does not follow through the same hole — he holds it from outside, so anyone rotating in to trade you walks into his angle. His 55.6% headshot rate is worth far more on a held angle than on an entry.

attack.then: Every reinforced wall in the plan is a dead end. Go through soft walls, existing doors or a hatch instead, and expect to fight into the site rather than through it.
attack.needs: hard breach|hard-breach|breach charge|reinforced wall|reinforced hatch|selma|exothermic|open the wall|opens the wall

attack.job: You kill the jammer or the electric claw before the breach, and you say it out loud when it is down.
attack.label: Utility clear
attack.have: Jammers, electric claws and cams can be removed before the breach.
attack.missing: No answer to a jammer or an electrified wall.
attack.then: A single Mute or Bandit stops the whole breach. Find the gadget with a drone and shoot it, or pick a wall they have not covered.

attack.job: You find the roamer and the anchor before anyone commits, and you keep one drone alive for the entry.
attack.label: Intel
attack.have: You can find the roamer and the anchor before committing.
attack.missing: You are entering blind past the drone phase.
attack.then: Clear behind you before you touch a wall. Keep one drone alive for the entry — a dead drone phase is how a two-man site turns into a flank.

attack.job: You make the rotates and the extra sightlines — open the angle the anchor is not expecting.
attack.label: Soft breach
attack.have: You can make your own rotates, sightlines and vertical holes.
attack.missing: You are limited to the doors and windows already there.
attack.then: Both entries are known to the defenders. Expect the anchor pre-aimed on them — take the fight from an angle rather than walking the obvious lane.
attack.needs: soft wall|soft breach|open the floor|vertical|make a hole|shoot through

attack.job: You break the anchor sightline before anyone steps into the plant lane. Shield or flash first, bodies second.
attack.label: Cover
attack.have: Someone can hold an angle open without winning a duel first.
attack.missing: Every angle has to be taken with a body.
attack.then: Do not dry-peek the plant lane. Use smoke or a flash to break the anchor sightline before anyone steps into it.
attack.needs: shield|hold the angle|plant lane|open the angle|cover the plant

defense.job: You keep the reinforced walls alive — electrics and jammers on the wall they want, placed in prep.
defense.label: Breach denial
defense.have: The reinforced walls in the plan can actually be defended.
defense.then: Every reinforced wall opens on their schedule. Reinforce for angles you can shoot rather than walls you cannot hold, and plan to fight after the breach, not before it.
defense.needs: jammer|electrif|electric|claw|denies a breach|deny the breach|gc90|shock wire

defense.job: You kill their drones early so they never map the site. Jammers down in prep, then anchor.
defense.label: Intel denial
defense.have: Their drones die before they map the site.
defense.missing: They will see your setup in full before the action phase.
defense.then: Assume they know where you are. Move after the drone phase — the spot you set up in is the spot they cleared.

defense.job: You cover the lanes nobody is standing in. Traps on the flank, not on the door someone already watches.
defense.label: Traps
defense.have: Flanks and unwatched entries cost them something without a body there.
defense.missing: Every lane needs a real person watching it.
defense.then: With two of you there are more entries than guns. Give up the far lane deliberately and hold the two that reach the defuser instead of spreading thin.

defense.job: You are the eyes — cams placed in prep covering approaches nobody is standing in, then call from them. You do not chase what you see.
defense.label: Intel
defense.have: You can watch approaches you are not standing in.
defense.missing: You only know what you can see.
defense.then: The default cams are all you have, so use them in prep and call from sound after that. Do not rotate on a guess.

defense.job: You eat the grenades aimed at the anchor. Place it covering the spot people actually stand.
defense.label: Projectile denial
defense.have: Grenades and breach charges thrown at your setup get eaten.
defense.missing: A single frag or impact clears your anchor spot.
defense.then: Do not hold a static angle they can grenade. Play off the spot, not on it, and reposition after the first utility comes in.

defense.job: You make sure the first trade does not lose the site — hold with the second gun, heal or shield after it.
defense.label: Anchor support
defense.have: A trade or a bad opening does not immediately lose the site.
defense.missing: The first death is a straight 2-on-1.
defense.then: Never take a duel you did not choose. Trade only when the second gun is already looking at the same hole.

B.label: Basement
B.why: Everything arrives from above — down the stairs or through a hatch. Denial on the ceiling and traps on the drop are worth more here than anything watching a door.
B.check: Find the hatches into this site in prep. If there are none, drop the electric denial and put that pick into another gun.

1F.label: Ground floor
1F.why: Pressure comes from outside AND from the floor above, so there are more ways in than you have bodies. Closing entries and slowing the push beats trying to watch them all.
1F.check: Count the outside entries before you reinforce. Anything you cannot watch should be barricaded or trapped, not left open.

2F.label: Top floor
2F.why: They rappel to your windows and push up the stairs, so the fight is same-floor and from below. Traps on windows and vault points pay more than ceiling denial.
2F.check: Check whether anything above you opens into this site. If nothing does, no reinforcement or gadget should be pointing up.

3F.label: Top floor
3F.why: They rappel to your windows and push up the stairs, so the fight is same-floor and from below. Traps on windows and vault points pay more than ceiling denial.
3F.check: Check whether anything above you opens into this site. If nothing does, no reinforcement or gadget should be pointing up.

attack.name: Default
changes: Full drone phase, clear utility, breach, enter together.
This is the baseline. Everything below is a change FROM it.
attack.why: They have no read on you yet. Take the version with the most information.

attack.name: Same plan, different face
attack.lead: They now expect pressure from where you came last round.
changes: Take a different spawn. Same site, same operators, same breach — approach from another side of the building.
Drone the side you used last round anyway. If someone is holding it, that is a body not defending the site.
Breach the opposite face of the site if there is one, or the same wall from the other end of the room.
attack.why: The cheapest possible change. Their setup rotated toward your last approach, and rotating costs them more than it costs you.

attack.name: Fast hit
attack.lead: Hit before the setup is finished.
changes: Skip the full drone phase. One drone in, find the anchor, go.
Take the entry with your faster operators — this is the round the fraggers lead, not the utility.
Accept you will not clear the roamer. Leave one body watching the flank instead of hunting it.
Plant early and play the post-plant with the clock on your side.
attack.why: A defense that beat you on a slow default has been rewarded for setting up deep. Arriving before the reinforcements and gadgets are down takes that away.

attack.name: Fake and late plant
attack.lead: Make noise where you are not going.
changes: Commit real noise to one entry — a charge, a breach, a body they can hear — then take a different one.
Do not plant on contact. Trade, back out, and let them rotate to the noise.
Plant late, with under thirty seconds, and defend the defuser rather than the room.
Whoever faked is now the flank watch, not part of the entry.
attack.why: Beats a defense that has started pre-aiming your entry. Their read is now a liability — they are looking at a doorway nobody is walking through.

defense.name: Default
changes: Reinforce in the written order, anchor holds, support calls.
This is the baseline. Everything below is a change FROM it.
defense.why: They have no read on you yet. Take the version with the strongest setup.

defense.name: Same setup, different bodies
defense.lead: They droned your positions last round. Keep the setup, move the people.
changes: Reinforce identically — the walls were right, they are not the thing that got read.
Both of you set up in prep as normal, then move before the action phase starts.
Swap roles: whoever anchored now takes the short roam, and the roamer holds the site.
Hold a different angle onto the same entry. Not a different room — a different line into it.
defense.why: The cheapest possible change, and it beats the most common read: they cleared the corner you sat in, and you are not in it.

defense.name: Early pressure
defense.lead: Meet them before they are set.
changes: One of you pushes out early for information and a possible pick, then comes straight back. One angle, one trade.
Kill drones aggressively in the first twenty seconds instead of saving utility.
The other body does not move — this only works if the site is still held while it happens.
If the early push gets a kill, collapse back and play the man advantage. Do not chase a second.
defense.why: Beats a team running a slow default. They are used to walking to the site unopposed; a body where they did not expect one costs them the whole setup phase.

defense.name: Give the room, take the retake
defense.lead: They have beaten you on entry twice. Stop contesting the entry.
changes: Set up off-site, not in it. Let them come in and let them plant.
Hold the angles they have to cross AFTER the plant, not the ones they cross to get in.
Do not trade at the doorway. The whole round is the retake.
One of you covers the defuser line, one covers their re-entry, and neither of you is where they cleared.
defense.why: Beats a team with a working entry. You cannot out-aim a coordinated push into a room they have solved — but a post-plant retake against a spread-out attack is a different fight.
